name: Singapore Institute of Technology
description: The Singapore Institute of Technology is a public university established in 2009 and granted Autonomous University status in 2014, with its main campus in Punggol. It offers applied, industry-focused degrees in engineering, health sciences, infocomm technology, business and design, including programmes run with overseas partner universities.
whyIncluded: One of Singapore's Ministry of Education (MOE)-funded Autonomous Universities, and the main local applied-degree pathway for polytechnic graduates who would otherwise consider overseas study.

programmes.name: Bachelor of Engineering with Honours in Electrical and Electronic Engineering
programmes.notes: SIT charges per credit, fixed for the AY2026 intake cohort: SC S$131.00, PR S$225.00, international (non-ASEAN, MOE Tuition Grant) S$371.69 per credit (ASEAN S$324.82; non-subsidised S$575.52). Annual figure = per-credit fee x 60 credits (240-credit, 4-year programme). SC/PR fees exclude GST (subsidised by MOE); international fees include 9% GST. 2025 history: AY2025 schedule (SC S$130.00, PR S$225.00, IS S$371.69 per credit). 2024 history from the AY2024 schedule (SC S$127.50, PR S$225.00, IS S$366.24 per credit). Compulsory fees = AY2026 miscellaneous fees of S$88.50 per trimester (SC/PR) or S$121.70 per trimester (international), both incl. 9% GST, x 3 trimesters a year (full-time programme rate on SIT's undergraduate tuition-fees page, read via a reader proxy on 2026-10-01 because the HTML is bot-protected); the fee schedule PDF itself lists tuition only. History rows carry tuition only; the current miscellaneous fee is applied to them.

programmes.name: Master of Science in Electrical and Electronic Engineering
programmes.notes: Per-credit fees fixed for the AY2026 postgraduate intake cohort: SC S$156.50 and PR S$318.00 (MOE-subsidised, excl. GST); international students pay the non-subsidised rate of S$641.47 per credit incl. 9% GST.
